A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, simulations, proofs, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data experiments on OLS data dropping, including one-outlier, Simpson’s paradox, poor-conditioning, and greedy-failure examples, with numerical results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulations and reports revised outlier diagnostics and additional inlier results in Appendix D, Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same AMIP, Additive One-Exact/Additive 1sN, and greedy procedures. Expanded explanations and corrections to supporting algebra do not introduce a new algorithm component or change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OLS slope changes using the same one-outlier, Simpson’s paradox, poor-conditioning, adversarial greedy-failure, and modified-geometry scenarios. The revised diagnostics remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same four approximation methods. One-Exact and 1sN terminology describes equivalent computations in these OLS experiments. Newly discussed related methods are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported background sample from 4,999 to 1,000 points and the outlier location from (100,100) to (1e6,1e6). The latter reconciles the description with Table 1, which already specified 1e6 in v2. Table 4 also changes its tested outlier positions. These reported-setting revisions do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2’s Table 4 diagnoses only the outlier. v4 revises that analysis and adds Table 5 tracking the most influential ordinary point, directly examining when its score exceeds the outlier’s. The detailed multi-outlier and geometric-perturbation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its own simulations. Additional diagnostic rows do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. Table 4 replaces diagnostic values; for example, the influence score at x=100 changes from 9.78e-3 to 1.64e-1. Table 5 adds ordinary-point results. These are revised or newly reported diagnostics under revised settings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The vanishing-influence proof in Proposition C.1, now D.1, corrects a missing inverse, the Sherman–Morrison sign, matrix transposes, and powers of lambda. Its assumptions and conclusion remain unchanged, as do the other principal propositions and approximation-error analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract’s failure claims and the recommendation to use Greedy One-Exact with diagnostic visualization remain. The introduction refines the novelty claim by recognizing Hu et al.’s contemporaneous systematic study and distinguishing conclusion changes from exact influential-subset recovery.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 explicitly states that realistic non-adversarial greedy failures have not been identified. Section 4.1 specifies Type 1 errors when describing the theoretical implication, and Appendix D.2 expands the explanation of misranking through comparisons between outlier and ordinary-point influence factors.

D1.justification: New Appendix A provides a repository link described as containing all reproduction scripts. New Appendix F reports an Apple M1 Pro CPU, 16 GB RAM, and approximately 5–10 seconds per experiment. These are new access and compute disclosures, not established changes to execution.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning relative to Hu et al., comparing objectives, masking explanations, and theoretical assumptions. It adds linear-regression usage, Data Shapley, and datamodels references. Appendix B also expands the distinction from data attribution and substantially revises the discussion of guaranteed auditing and lower-bound algorithms.

P1.justification: The introduction and selected algorithm, intuition, and discussion paragraphs are revised, while the main narrative sequence remains. References are alphabetized, headings standardized, and new Code and Compute appendices added. The former Discussion appendix is renamed Limitations.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised axes, fitted-line displays, labels, and an outlier-panel inset. Table 4 is redesigned and Table 5 added. Figures 2–8 are reused, with several appendix displays relocated; the overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs algebra in the outlier proof, aligns Figure 1’s outlier location with Table 1, clarifies positioning and applicability limits, and adds reproducibility information. These improve the core explanation while retaining the main comparisons. The gain is limited by reporting problems: Section 4.1 retains a 0.02% deletion fraction after changing to 1,000 background points, and new Table 5 contains factors that do not consistently reproduce its reported influence scores.
